svg.text: Old Agora apps vs this kit — what they had, what we have now
Audited from the four legacy projects (2026-07-24). Key finding: despite the name, the old apps had NO real captions at all.

g.text: Join a channel
Type a 6-digit code; sandbox had a custom
agora:// deeplink. No web links.
One parser, three forms: bare id/code, vck:// deeplink,
https web link — each with ?lang, validated live in the UI,
round-tripping invite generators. (12 tests)
Live captions
NONE. Zero STT, zero caption UI, zero
translation — only a speech audio profile flag.
Real pipeline: ordered translation, per-language fan-out,
zero-latency interim captions (italic…), bounded queues,
failure fallback — never drops a line. (31 tests)
Roles & speaking rights
admins array ⇒ Agora publisher; everyone else
force-muted client-side (bypassable).
host / speaker / listener enforced in the channel core —
a listener's publish is rejected by code, not by a mute
flag; host promotes explicitly.
Member language
A free-text group field, written once,
never read by any logic. Dead data.
Live routing: every member declares a language, captions
arrive translated per member; the pipeline retargets as
languages join and leave.
Presence / host loss
Host-offline timer ⇒ hard "Host went offline",
room effectively over.
Heartbeat deadline for EVERY member; a lost host is
expired like anyone else and captions keep flowing —
the channel survives its creator.
Security & tokens
App certificate hard-coded in the client;
tokens minted on-device (leakable), 24h expiry.
No vendor cloud, no embedded secrets: E2E identity +
signed config + keychain storage already in the kit's
security packages (170 tests).
Hard-network survival
Whatever Agora's cloud does — opaque,
no client-side degradation model at all.
Full survival stack: 6-rung quality ladder to 6 kbps voice,
degraded phase, voice-note fallback, call memory replay,
path-health reconnects — all soak-tested.
Dependency & cost
Agora RTC cloud + Firebase per room-minute —
vendor bill and vendor availability.
Own WebRTC + own signaling; captions ride the call's
existing data channel at a few bytes per line.

svg.text: What the old apps still have that we haven't wired yet (honest gaps):
a real STT engine (ours is an injectable seam), multi-device channel transport (needs the relay/real devices), Google sign-in, payments/paywall, emoji reactions.
